notes.japanese: 子供の瞬間もぢっとしてない、小鳥のやうに愛らしい様子を見つめた
notes.problem: Rationalisation by misattachment: never-still belongs to the child in Japanese, not to her gaze.
notes.span: gazed at the child, never still for an instant, lovely as a little bird.
notes.suggestion: gazed at the child — never still for an instant, lovely as a little bird.
notes.sureness: Sure; the Japanese relative clause modifies the child's state, not her eyes.

notes.japanese: ジャガ芋の無味な、かゝはりのない冷やかな不味さが
notes.problem: Clarification: adds 'with her' where Japanese leaves what it is unrelated to unsaid.
notes.suggestion: And the tasteless, unrelated, cold badness of the potato gave her a quiet, lonely, far-removed heart.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; crux says keep its unrelated ordinariness, a check of かかりのない usage would settle it.

notes.japanese: たゞ静かに安らかにぢっと微笑をつゞけてゐるばかりであって
notes.problem: Expansion: invents a fixed gaze where ぢっと steadies the continuing smile.
notes.suggestion: But teller and listener alike only went on smiling on, quietly and peacefully, steadily, and they did not move at all.
notes.sureness: Sure; there is no gaze noun in the sentence.

notes.japanese: さうだ。あの日があるのだ。あのすべてがなつかしみと許しと、安らかさに変る日があるのだった。
notes.problem: Destroyed rhythm of time: present interior certainty turned to past and conditional.
notes.span: There was that day. There was the day when all would be changed into nostalgia and forgiveness, and peace.
notes.suggestion: Yes. There is that day. There is the day when all changes into nostalgia and forgiveness, and peace.
notes.sureness: Sure about present あるのだ; house tense policy for interior present would settle exact wording.

notes.japanese: 一日々々の苦しみや悲しみがなんだらう。一日々々の疲れやなやみがなんだらう。
notes.problem: Same tense flattening: dismissive present-future made past.
notes.span: What were the suffering and sorrow of day by day? What were the weariness and trouble of day by day?
notes.suggestion: What are the suffering and sorrow of day by day? What are the weariness and trouble of day by day?
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; なんだらう is present conjecture, not past.

notes.japanese: くり〳〵と肥ってる女の子だった
notes.problem: Expansion: inserts eyes where Japanese has only round plumpness.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure there is no eye word; period use of くりくり would confirm.

notes.problem: Normalisation destroying evidence: neutral Baby hides 坊や used for a 女の子, flagged as open fork.
notes.suggestion: she said, 'Boy,' firmly, — keep 坊や literally also at p28 and p30, with note, so the editor sees the fork.
notes.sureness: Sure about the loss; unsure which side editor wants, needs fork decision not silent smoothing.

notes.problem: Expansion: adds little where Japanese says only her hands.
notes.span: put it into her little hands.
notes.sureness: Sure; nothing for little in the clause.

notes.japanese: 遠い心が静かに思出してゐるのだった
notes.problem: Rationalisation: distant heart as remembering subject replaced by she with heart as instrument.
notes.span: And with a distant heart she quietly remembered
notes.suggestion: And a distant heart quietly remembered the quiet tear-filled days...
notes.sureness: Sure on grammar; whether English can bear heart as subject is for the desk.

notes.japanese: 總てが、總ての事が懐しみと許しとに変る事だらう
notes.problem: Rationalisation into passive be changed where Japanese intransitive changes by itself.
notes.span: be changed into nostalgia and forgiveness.
notes.suggestion: would everything, all things, change into nostalgia and forgiveness.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure; 変る is intransitive here, no agent implied.

notes.japanese: 俺たちはいろ〳〵苦労したなァ
notes.problem: Flattened vernacular and ennoblement: rough masculine俺たち turned to polite you and I.
notes.span: But we have been through a good deal, you and I.
notes.suggestion: But we've been through a lot, we have.
notes.sureness: Medium sure; register judgment, but 俺 and なァ mark plain young husband speech.

notes.problem: Ennoblement into archaism where Japanese is plain bodily.
notes.sureness: Sure that give suck is period archaism English readers will hear as biblical.

notes.japanese: 手持ぶさたのやうにスプーンを持って立ってる子供を見た
notes.problem: Clarification settling an ambiguous attachment as the child's idleness.
notes.suggestion: looked, as if at a loss himself, at the child standing holding the spoon — leave whose idleness open.
notes.sureness: Unsure; Japanese syntax lets it hang on either man or child, needs a second Japanese check.

notes.japanese: 何物にか気をとられたやうに
notes.problem: Ennoblement into unnatural heed-taken phrasing for plain distractedness.
notes.span: as if her heed had been taken by something,
notes.sureness: Sure that current phrasing no good writer would sign; exact shade of 気をとられる needs context.

data.say: Supper holds, but vision, potato and day-by-day refrains need tense, repetition and added-word fixes before the desk weighs them.
